claim: PLK-1 localises to the spindle poles during prometaphase I in C. elegans oocytes.
source: PLK-1 localises to the spindle poles (Figure 1C, blue arrows), chromosome arms (Figure 1A and C, yellow arrows), and midbivalent region between the homologous chromosomes (Figure 1A and C, magenta arrow) during prometaphase I.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 1C showing PLK-1 localization.

claim: PLK-1 localises to chromosome arms during prometaphase I in C. elegans oocytes.
source: PLK-1 localises to the spindle poles (Figure 1C, blue arrows), chromosome arms (Figure 1A and C, yellow arrows), and midbivalent region between the homologous chromosomes (Figure 1A and C, magenta arrow) during prometaphase I.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 1C showing PLK-1 localization.

claim: PLK-1 localises to the midbivalent region between homologous chromosomes during prometaphase I in C. elegans oocytes.
source: PLK-1 localises to the spindle poles (Figure 1C, blue arrows), chromosome arms (Figure 1A and C, yellow arrows), and midbivalent region between the homologous chromosomes (Figure 1A and C, magenta arrow) during prometaphase I.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 1C showing PLK-1 localization.

claim: PLK-1 is enriched in the central spindle during late anaphase in C. elegans oocytes.

evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 1C.

claim: Acute inhibition of PLK-1 with 10 µM 3IB-PP1 leads to drastic spindle defects with no observable bipolar spindle formation in C. elegans oocytes.
source: Addition of 10 µM 3IB-PP1 between 5 and 15 min before dissection and imaging of oocytes allowed us to bypass the NEBD defect, and six bivalents were easily identifiable within the newly fertilised oocyte (Figure 1E, yellow arrows). Under these conditions PLK-1as inhibition led to drastic spindle defects with no observable bipolar spindle formation and no consequent chromosome segregation was observed, indicating that PLK-1 is involved in spindle assembly and/or stability during oocyte meiosis (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 1E showing spindle defects.

claim: PLK-1 is involved in spindle assembly and/or stability during oocyte meiosis in C. elegans.
source: Under these conditions PLK-1as inhibition led to drastic spindle defects with no observable bipolar spindle formation and no consequent chromosome segregation was observed, indicating that PLK-1 is involved in spindle assembly and/or stability during oocyte meiosis (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing spindle defects upon PLK-1 inhibition.

claim: Approximately 62% of oocytes treated with 1 µM 3IB-PP1 had seemingly bipolar spindles.
source: Under these conditions, ~62% of oocytes had seemingly bipolar spindles and chromosomes remained somewhat associated with the spindle, although chromosome alignment was still affected in 78% of oocytes (≥2 misaligned chromosomes, Figure 1F and G).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by quantitative data in Figure 1G.

claim: Chromosome alignment was affected in 78% of oocytes treated with 1 µM 3IB-PP1.
source: Under these conditions, ~62% of oocytes had seemingly bipolar spindles and chromosomes remained somewhat associated with the spindle, although chromosome alignment was still affected in 78% of oocytes (≥2 misaligned chromosomes, Figure 1F and G).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by quantitative data in Figure 1G.

claim: PLK-1 participates in chromosome alignment in a manner that is at least partially independent of its roles in overall spindle assembly and/or stability.
source: We then used the pole marker ASPM-1 to allow proper characterisation of spindle bipolarity under these conditions and confirmed that even when two ASPM-1 poles are clearly discerned (Figure 1H, blue arrows), chromosome alignment fails (Figure 1H, yellow arrows). Hence, it appears that PLK-1 participates in chromosome alignment in a manner that is at least partially independent of its roles in overall spindle assembly and/or stability.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental data showing chromosome alignment defects even when spindle bipolarity is maintained.

claim: RNAi-mediated depletion of BUB-1 led to the loss of PLK-1 from the midbivalent in C. elegans oocytes.

claim: PLK-1 signal at chromosome arms remained unaffected after BUB-1 depletion.
